question: Why is a game that says no AI was used at the top of itch.io's Popular ranking in Epic's AI game jam?

rungs.question: Why could a game made without AI enter a jam built around AI tools?
rungs.answer: Epic's rules invited any AI tools but did not require them. The jam's own FAQ answers 'Do I have to use AI?' with 'No', and the rules say how much AI a team uses does not change eligibility or score.

evidence.quote: Using them is optional and doesn’t affect judging.
However, using AI was not mandatory, and the rules explicitly state that the extent of AI usage will not affect a game’s eligibility or score.
Epic Games' 2026 AI MegaJam offers around $65,000 in cash prizes, and Epic has clarified that using AI tools is optional.

counter.text: TweakTown reports the first wording read as if AI were required: "Epic initially worded the rules to make AI use sound mandatory, then quickly clarified that it is completely optional." The Official Rules and Epic's own news post (403) were not read.

rungs.question: Why does LSD:FIH sit at the top of the Popular ranking?
rungs.answer: itch.io's Popular sort is its own algorithm built on engagement such as page views, downloads and players, and it is separate from the jam's judging. The game's page shows 451 ratings averaging 4.9, and it is first on the entries list as fetched.

evidence.quote: According to itch.io founder Leaf Corcoran, the algorithm takes into account various organic engagement metrics, including page views, downloads, and player numbers.
PolyCube’s LSD: FIH is currently the most popular game on the 2026 Epic AI MegaJam itch.io submissions page

counter.text: The ranking is not the result: "Note that the platform’s popularity ranking does not determine the winners of the game jam" (Automaton). Only Automaton describes how the algorithm works, citing Corcoran second hand, so engagement as the cause is not confirmed by itch.io itself in what was read. The jam page also shows 2,778 entries against the 2,782 Epic announced.

rungs.question: Why did so many players engage with this one entry?
rungs.answer: Two reasons appear side by side. The developer made the lack of AI the pitch, and commenters cheer it as human-made. Both outlets also say the game itself is fun. Neither source measures how much each reason weighs.

evidence.quote: This game is proof that humans are better at creating games than AI.
These circumstances have no doubt contributed to LSD:FIH’s popularity, although the game itself has also earned praise for its simple yet entertaining design.
there is a concern that LSD: FIH may simply be a protest vote

counter.text: Kotaku's reviewer played it and found the game good on its own terms: "So, just in case, I played LSD: FIH, and lemme tell you…this game kinda slaps." No source separates protest from enjoyment.

rungs.question: Why would a no-AI stance draw attention in this jam in particular?
rungs.answer: The sources describe a backlash against heavily AI-made games and against Epic's own AI-first turn, and the jam is backed by AI companies including Anthropic, Google and OpenAI. A human-made game winning the crowd inside that setting is the contrast both outlets write about.

evidence.quote: given the internet’s well-documented distaste for Epic Games’ new “AI first” pivot in the last few years
Against this backdrop, developers and players alike have become increasingly critical of game development that relies heavily on AI.
Supported by Claude, Google, OpenAI, SpaceXSI, AMD, Diversion, fal, Hyper3D, Intel, Meshy,

counter.text: Within the jam itself the no-AI angle is not unique: the entries list also carries an entry titled "THIS GAME IS AI SLOP", and no source says how many of the 2,782 entries used AI or how they rank. Searched only the six pages read.

landing.shows: Epic's rules let a game with no AI compete on equal terms, and itch.io's engagement-driven Popular sort, which is separate from judging, has put such a game first. The sources tie its pull partly to a backlash against AI-made games and Epic's AI push, and partly to the game being fun, without saying which matters more.
landing.open_question: If the most engaged-with entry in an AI jam is the one that refused AI, what is the jam actually measuring?
